relations.rationale: Both describe Hugo's actions before rehearsal but neither implies the other.
Taking a back row spot has no bearing on relative height compared to Kai.
Sitting at the back row doesn't imply anything about helping stack chairs later.
Hugo adjusting his music stand has nothing to do with Yara's and Zeno's class assignments.
Hugo's stand adjustment is unrelated to Milo's tenure in the group.

If Yara and Milo share a class, and Milo is not in Zeno's class, this supports the idea that Yara is also not in Zeno's class, but it directly supports the claim about Milo, which is given as true here, so it's consistent but doesn't itself establish 19; but as a logical support A implies a shared class reduces likelihood Milo is with Zeno if we know Yara isn't, though here we don't know Yara's relation to Zeno, so it's weakly supportive at best.
Yara being in the same class as Milo doesn't determine her relation to Zeno.
Yara's classmate status with Milo has no bearing on how long Zeno has been in the choir.
Yara's class relation to Milo doesn't affect Kai's offer to lock up.
Yara's classmate status doesn't affect the scheduling of the next rehearsal.
Milo not being in Zeno's class doesn't determine whether Yara is in Zeno's class.
The pianist repeating the opening bars is consistent with and could explain why the sopranos struggled, suggesting difficulty in that passage.
The pianist's rehearsal actions have no bearing on Yara's class relationship with Zeno.
Running through opening bars twice doesn't relate to whether the next rehearsal is scheduled.
Yara's class relation to Zeno has nothing to do with Kai's offer to lock up.
Zeno joining only a year ago contrasts with Milo's long-standing membership, but these are independent facts about different people, not implying each other.
Hugo helping stack chairs is a separate act from Kai's offer to lock up, though both suggest helpfulness after rehearsal, they don't causally imply each other.
